questions.q: Air contains nearly 20% oxygen by volume. The volume of air needed for complete combustion of 100 mL of acetylene will be :
questions.s: $\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{2}$ + 5/2 $\text{O}_{2}$ → 2$\text{CO}_{2}$ + $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$. So 100 mL of $\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{2}$ needs 250 mL of oxygen. Air is 20% oxygen, so air needed = 250 × 5 = 1250 mL.

questions.q: Elements A and B form two compounds $\text{B}_{2}\text{A}_{3}$ and $\text{B}_{2}\text{A}$. 0.05 moles of $\text{B}_{2}\text{A}_{3}$ weigh 9.0 g and 0.10 mole of $\text{B}_{2}\text{A}$ weigh 10 g. Atomic weight of A and B are-
questions.s: Molar masses: $\text{B}_{2}\text{A}_{3}$ = 9.0/0.05 = 180 and $\text{B}_{2}\text{A}$ = 10/0.10 = 100. So 2B + 3A = 180 and 2B + A = 100. Subtracting gives 2A = 80, so A = 40 and B = 30.

questions.q: If $3.01\times10^{20}$ molecules are removed from 98 mg of $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$, then the number of moles of $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ left are :–
Which of the following has the highest mass ?
questions.s: Masses: 1 g atom of C = 12 g, half a mole of $\text{CH}_{4}$ = 8 g, 10 mL of water = 10 g, and $3.011\times10^{23}$ oxygen atoms (0.5 mol) = 8 g. So carbon is the heaviest.

questions.q: An oxide of metal M has 40% by mass of oxygen. Metal M has atomic mass of 24. The empirical formula of the oxide is
questions.s: In 100 g: O = 40/16 = 2.5 mol and M = 60/24 = 2.5 mol. The ratio is 1 : 1, so the formula is MO.

questions.q: A compound contains 38.8% C, 16.0% H and 45.2% N. The formula of the compound would be
questions.s: Moles: C = 38.8/12 = 3.23, H = 16/1 = 16, N = 45.2/14 = 3.23. The ratio C : H : N is 1 : 5 : 1, which is $\text{CH}_{5}\text{N}$, written as $\text{CH}_{3}\text{NH}_{2}$.

questions.q: 10 mL of gaseous hydrocarbon on combustion give 40 mL of $\text{CO}_{2}$(g) and 50 mL of $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ (vap.). The hydrocarbon is -
questions.s: Each molecule gives 40/10 = 4 $\text{CO}_{2}$, so it has 4 carbon atoms. It gives 50/10 = 5 $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$, so it has 10 hydrogen atoms. The formula is $\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{10}$.

questions.q: 500 mL of a gaseous hydrocarbon when burnt in excess of $\text{O}_{2}$ gave 2.5 L of $\text{CO}_{2}$ and 3.0 L of water vapours under same conditions. Molecular formula of the hydrocarbon is -
questions.s: $\text{CO}_{2}$ per hydrocarbon = 2.5/0.5 = 5, so 5 carbon atoms. $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ per hydrocarbon = 3.0/0.5 = 6, so 12 hydrogen atoms. The formula is $\text{C}_{5}\text{H}_{12}$.

questions.q: 1 L of a hydrocarbon weighs as much as one litre of $\text{CO}_{2}$ Under similar conditions. Then the molecular formula of the hydrocarbon is -
questions.s: Equal volumes under the same conditions have equal moles, so equal mass means equal molar mass. $\text{CO}_{2}$ is 44 g/mol, and $\text{C}_{3}\text{H}_{8}$ = 36 + 8 = 44 g/mol.

questions.q:
0.01 mole of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_{3}$) reacts with Ag to produce a gas whose volume at NTP is
2$\text{CHI}_{3}$ + 6Ag → $\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{2}$ + 6AgI(s)
questions.s: 2 mol of $\text{CHI}_{3}$ give 1 mol of $\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{2}$. So 0.01 mol gives 0.005 mol of $\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{2}$. Volume = 0.005 × 22400 = 112 mL.

questions.q: $\text{CaCO}_{3}$ is 90% pure. Volume of $\text{CO}_{2}$ collected at STP when 10 g of $\text{CaCO}_{3}$ is decomposed is -
questions.s: Pure $\text{CaCO}_{3}$ = 90% of 10 g = 9 g = 0.09 mol. $\text{CaCO}_{3}$ → CaO + $\text{CO}_{2}$ gives 0.09 mol of $\text{CO}_{2}$. Volume = 0.09 × 22.4 = 2.016 L.

questions.q: How many mole of magnesium phosphate, $\text{Mg}_{3}\text{(PO}_{4}\text{)}_{2}$ will contain 0.25 mole of oxygen atoms?
questions.s: One formula unit of $\text{Mg}_{3}\text{(PO}_{4}\text{)}_{2}$ has 8 oxygen atoms, so 1 mol has 8 mol of O atoms. Moles needed = 0.25/8 = $3.125\times10^{-2}$.

questions.q:
Percentage composition of an organic compound is as follows :
C=10.06, H=0.84 , Cl=89.10
Which of the following corresponds to its molecular formula if the vapour density is 60.0
questions.s: Moles: C = 0.838, H = 0.84, Cl = 89.10/35.5 = 2.51. The ratio is 1 : 1 : 3, giving $\text{CHCl}_{3}$. Its molar mass is 119.5, which matches 2 × 60 = 120.

questions.q: The ratio of masses of oxygen and nitrogen in a particular gaseous mixture is 1 : 4. The ratio of number of their molecule is
questions.s: Moles = mass/molar mass. Oxygen gives 1/32 and nitrogen gives 4/28 = 1/7. The ratio is 1/32 : 1/7 = 7 : 32.

questions.q:
23 g sodium metal reacts with water. Calculate the (a) volume of $\text{H}_{2}$ liberated at NTP (b) moles of $\text{H}_{2}$ liberated (c) weight of $\text{H}_{2}$ liberated.
2Na + 2$\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ → 2NaOH + $\text{H}_{2}$
questions.s: 23 g of Na is 1 mol. 2 mol of Na give 1 mol of $\text{H}_{2}$, so 1 mol gives 1/2 mol. That is 11.2 L at NTP and 1/2 × 2 = 1 g.

questions.q: Which of the following is a compound
questions.s: Marble is calcium carbonate ($\text{CaCO}_{3}$), a pure compound with a fixed ratio of elements. Graphite is an element, while steel and cement are mixtures.

questions.q: Calculate the number of atoms of chlorine in 2.08 gm of $\text{BaCl}_{2}$. (Atomic weight of Ba = 137, Cl = 35.5)
questions.s: Molar mass of $\text{BaCl}_{2}$ = 137 + 71 = 208. So 2.08 g = 0.01 mol. Each unit has 2 Cl atoms, so Cl atoms = 0.02 mol = $2\times10^{-2}\,N_A$.

questions.q: A container of volume V, contains 0.28 g of $\text{N}_{2}$ gas. If same volume of an unknown gas under similar condition of temperature and pressure weighs, 0.44 g, the molecular mass of the gas is
questions.s: Same volume, temperature and pressure means the same moles. $\text{N}_{2}$: 0.28/28 = 0.01 mol. So the unknown gas is 0.01 mol weighing 0.44 g, giving M = 0.44/0.01 = 44.

questions.q: 2.2 g of a compound of phosphorous and sulphur has 1.24 g of 'P' in it. Its empirical formula is -
questions.s: Sulphur = 2.2 − 1.24 = 0.96 g. Moles: P = 1.24/31 = 0.04 and S = 0.96/32 = 0.03. The ratio P : S is 4 : 3, so the formula is $\text{P}_{4}\text{S}_{3}$.

questions.q:
On analysis, a certain compound was found to contain iodine and oxygen in the ratio of 254 : 80. The formula of the compound is :
(At mass I = 127, O = 16)
questions.s: Moles: I = 254/127 = 2 and O = 80/16 = 5. The ratio 2 : 5 gives $\text{I}_{2}\text{O}_{5}$.

questions.q: What volume of oxygen gas ($\text{O}_{2}$) measured at 0°C and 1 atm, is needed to burn completely 1L, of propane gas ($\text{C}_{3}\text{H}_{8}$) measured under the same conditions:-
questions.s: $\text{C}_{3}\text{H}_{8}$ + 5$\text{O}_{2}$ → 3$\text{CO}_{2}$ + 4$\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$. Gas volumes follow mole ratios, so 1 L of propane needs 5 L of oxygen.

questions.q: Volume occupied by one molecule of water (density =1 g$cm^{-3}$) is :-
questions.s: 18 g of water has volume 18 $cm^{3}$ (density 1 g/$cm^{3}$) and holds $6.023\times10^{23}$ molecules. Volume per molecule = 18/$6.023\times10^{23}$ = $3.0\times10^{-23}$ $cm^{3}$.

questions.q:
How many moles of lead (II) chloride will be formed from a reaction between 6.5 g of PbO and 3.2 g of HCl ? (Atomic wt. of Pb=207)
PbO + 2HCl → $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ + $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$
questions.s: PbO = 6.5/223 = 0.029 mol. HCl = 3.2/36.5 = 0.088 mol, but 0.029 mol of PbO needs only 0.058 mol of HCl. So PbO is limiting and $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ = 0.029 mol.

questions.q: An organic compound contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Its elemental analysis gives C, 38.71% and H, 9.67%. The empirical formula of the compound would be :-
questions.s: O = 100 − 38.71 − 9.67 = 51.62%. Moles: C = 3.23, H = 9.67 and O = 3.23. The ratio is 1 : 3 : 1, so the formula is $\text{CH}_{3}\text{O}$.

questions.q: 10g of hydrogen and 64 g of oxygen were filled in a steel vessel and exploded. Amount of water produced in this reaction will be :-
questions.s: $\text{H}_{2}$ = 10/2 = 5 mol and $\text{O}_{2}$ = 64/32 = 2 mol. 2$\text{H}_{2}$ + $\text{O}_{2}$ → 2$\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ needs 2 mol of $\text{H}_{2}$ per mol of $\text{O}_{2}$, so oxygen limits. Water = 2 × 2 = 4 mol.

questions.q: The number of atoms in 0.1 mol of a triatomic gas is :- ($N_A = 6.02\times10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.s: Each molecule has 3 atoms. Atoms = 0.1 × 3 × $6.02\times10^{23}$ = $1.806\times10^{23}$.

questions.q: Which has the maximum number of molecules among the following?
questions.s: Moles: $\text{SO}_{2}$ = 64/64 = 1, $\text{CO}_{2}$ = 44/44 = 1, $\text{O}_{3}$ = 48/48 = 1 and $\text{H}_{2}$ = 8/2 = 4. $\text{H}_{2}$ has the most moles, so the most molecules.
